title: Door Before You Step
hook: Parked parallel. The door wants the bike lane.
scene: Clear cold dawn, a downtown curb, you already nailed the parallel — plow in line, wheels straight, one foot from the curb. The engine dies. Marisol is a dark shape in the left door glass, closing fast in the bike lane you just boxed with a door that has not opened yet. The Dutch reach is the far hand, look, then the latch. Opening the near hand is how a bike becomes a story.
decision: You are parked and a bike is in the glass. How do you open the door?

options.text: Open with the near hand and step out — you are already parked
options.result: The door takes the bike lane. Marisol has nowhere. Carbon and a pink panel. She goes down along the curb. Parked was not permission to throw a door into a lane.

options.text: Far hand on the latch so your body turns, look, then open a crack
options.result: You reach across. The turn puts the glass in your face. Marisol is a whole bike, not a smear. You wait. She passes. The door opens on empty paint. She does not have to lift.

options.text: Crack the door two inches without looking so she has to slow
options.result: The two inches is still a wall. She swerves into the travel lane. A van has to lift. You taught the curb that a parked car gets to shove.

options.text: Wait until you cannot see her, then open fast and get it over with
options.result: Losing her in the glass is not a clear. She is in the blind stretch along the door. You open into a bike you decided was gone. The curb takes both of you.

debrief: After a parallel park, check the bike lane before the door moves. Far hand on the latch turns you into the glass. Marisol was already in the glass.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: After parallel parking, check for bikes and people before opening the door; use the far-hand reach so the body turns to look.
